mainTopic: The limit of מלקות, three readings of 'עיבור החדש בשלשה', and the stages of judges for עיבור השנה
overview: The amud opens at the end of a discussion about מלקות. Someone asks why the court doesn't give one more lash, since the man is still alive when it lands. רב אשי answers from 'ונקלה אחיך לעיניך': after the whipping he must still be 'your brother', meaning alive. Next the גמרא asks why the משנה says 'עיבור החדש בשלשה', since a month gets longer by itself if nobody declares the new month. אביי changes the wording to 'קידוש החדש', but רבא objects. Three readings that keep the word 'עיבור' follow. רבא says קידוש on the 30th day needs three, like רבי אלעזר בן צדוק. רב נחמן says קידוש on the 31st day needs three, like פלימו. רב אשי says the משנה means only the calculation, like רבי אליעזר, who holds that months are never formally sanctified. Then a ברייתא explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's stages for עיבור השנה: three judges begin, five debate, and seven decide, with a majority 'no' ending the process at any stage. The numbers three, five and seven are tied either to ברכת כהנים or to the king's officials, and רב יוסף's ברייתא backs the second view. A short exchange between אביי and רב יוסף follows. The amud ends with a memory aid and the start of a ברייתא on when a year may be extended, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not give one more lash?
steps.stepSummary: A questioner asks why the court does not give the person twenty-one lashes. Even if he dies from the last one, he was alive when it was struck.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the court give him twenty-one lashes, and if he dies from that last one, let him die. After all, when they strike that lash, they are striking the back of a living man.
steps.whatsHappening: The text begins in the middle of a discussion about how many lashes (מלקות) a person may get. Someone challenges the limit and asks: why not add one more lash?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that the doctors' estimate shows he will still be alive after the twentieth lash. So the twenty-first lash lands on a living person. The questioner argues there should be no problem, even if that last lash kills him.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them strike him
Twenty-one
Let him die
On the back of a living person

phrases.english: Let them strike him twenty-one lashes,
and if he dies from that one, let him die,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the extra, twenty-first lash.

phrases.english: for when they strike
it is on the back of a living person that they strike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the previous עמוד about estimating how many lashes a person can survive.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the lashes stop below the estimated number the person can bear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each lash, including the last one, lands on a living person, so the court is never striking a dead man.

steps.title: He must still be 'your brother' after the lashes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers from the פסוק 'ונקלה אחיך לעיניך'. The person must still be 'your brother' after the whipping, and if he dies, he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The פסוק says, 'and your brother will be dishonored before your eyes.' This means that after he is whipped, I need him to still be 'your brother'. If he dies, he no longer is.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge with a פסוק. The Torah calls the person 'your brother' even after the lashes, so he must come out of it alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The questioner only looked at whether the man is alive when each lash lands. רב אשי says the Torah also cares about the result after the whipping is finished. The word 'אחיך' tells us the person must survive, so we may not give a lash that might end his life.

keyTerms.meaning: And your brother will be dishonored before your eyes
After he has been whipped
And there isn't (he no longer is)

steps.whatToRemember: The lashes must stop at a number the person can survive, because the Torah still calls him 'אחיך' after the punishment is over.

phrases.english: He said to him: The verse says
"and your brother will be dishonored before your eyes"
after he was whipped, I need him to be "your brother", and he isn't.
phrases.notes: If he died from the lash, he is no longer 'your brother' standing there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since every lash lands on a living man, an extra lash that might kill should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק requires that he still be 'your brother' (alive) after the whipping, so no lash that may kill him is given.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: lengthening the month needs three judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: עיבור החדש is done by three judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: The intercalation (lengthening) of the month is done by three judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will look closely at its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עיבור החדש' means making the outgoing month 30 days long instead of 29. Then the new month starts on the 31st day. The משנה says this needs a בית דין of three.

keyTerms.meaning: Lengthening the month by an extra (30th) day
With three judges

phrases.english: The intercalation of the month is with three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of מלקות to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיבור החדש requires a בית דין of three.

steps.title: Why would lengthening a month need judges?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה said 'עיבור', not 'חישוב' or 'קידוש'. It asks why judges are needed for this, since a month becomes longer by itself if nobody declares the new month.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה does not say 'calculation', and it does not say 'sanctification'. It says 'intercalation'. But why do we need judges for that? Let them just not sanctify the new month, and the old month will become longer by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks carefully at the exact word the משנה chose and finds a problem with it. Lengthening a month seems to happen automatically, so why would it need a בית דין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the בית דין does nothing on the 30th day, that day simply belongs to the old month, and the new month starts the next day. So 'עיבור' looks like doing nothing at all, and doing nothing should not need three judges. The question is aimed at the wording of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The calculation of the month
Formally declaring the new month holy
It does not teach (say)
And let it become longer by itself

steps.confusionAlert: עיבור החדש here is not adding a whole month to the year. It means adding one day to a month, making it 30 days instead of 29.

phrases.aramaic: חִישּׁוּב לָא קָתָנֵי, קִידּוּשׁ לָא קָתָנֵי,
phrases.english: It does not teach 'calculation', it does not teach 'sanctification',
but rather 'intercalation'.
Let them not sanctify it, and it will be intercalated by itself?
phrases.notes: If nobody declares the new month on day 30, the old month just turns out 30 days long.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִישּׁוּב לָא קָתָנֵי, קִידּוּשׁ לָא קָתָנֵי, אֶלָּא עִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lengthening the month happens automatically when no קידוש is done, so it should not need a בית דין of three.

steps.title: אביי: read it as 'sanctification of the month'
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה should be read as 'קידוש החדש', declaring the new month, which really does need a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Teach it as 'the sanctification of the month' is done by three judges.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי solves the problem by changing the wording of the משנה. He reads it as 'קידוש' instead of 'עיבור'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Declaring the new month is an active act of the בית דין, so it makes sense that it needs three judges. With this change, the problem from the last step goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Declaring the new month

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Teach: 'the sanctification of the month'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is talking about lengthening the month, which happens by itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is really talking about קידוש החדש, which needs an active בית דין.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says, according to רבי מאיר, that קידוש החדש and עיבור השנה are done by three, which supports אביי's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: The sanctification of the month and the intercalation of the year are done by three judges. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up אביי. That ברייתא uses the exact words 'קידוש החדש'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a ברייתא lists 'קידוש החדש' as needing three judges, אביי's reading of the משנה matches a known teaching. This makes his change of wording more convincing.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this
Adding a month to the year (a leap year)

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
The sanctification of the month and the intercalation of the year are with three,
the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer in step 5.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the name of רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבא: but the משנה says 'עיבור'!
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to אביי: the משנה clearly says 'עיבור', so we cannot just change it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: But the משנה teaches 'intercalation'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer. He does not want to change the words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's word is 'עיבור', and the גמרא already pointed out that it did not say 'קידוש'. Changing it is a forced answer, so רבא looks for an explanation that keeps the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, (the text) …

phrases.english: Rava said:
But it teaches "intercalation"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's change of wording from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading of 'קידוש' in place of 'עיבור'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says 'עיבור', so we should not change its words.

steps.title: רבא: three judges for קידוש on the 'day of עיבור'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'עיבור' means the 30th day. קידוש on that day needs three judges. After that day, no קידוש is done at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Sanctifying the month on the day of intercalation needs three judges. After the day of intercalation, there is no sanctification.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own explanation that keeps the word 'עיבור'. He reads it as the name of a day, the 30th, and not as the act of lengthening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the new month is declared on the 30th day, a בית דין of three must do קידוש. If the month is lengthened and the new month starts on the 31st, no קידוש is done. So the משנה's 'עיבור' points to the day on which קידוש matters.

keyTerms.meaning: On the day of עיבור (the 30th day)
After the day of עיבור (the 31st day)
There is no sanctification

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Sanctification on the day of intercalation is with three,
phrases.notes: The 'day of עיבור' is day 30, which would become the extra day if the month is lengthened.

phrases.english: after intercalation there is no sanctification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 in a new way after rejecting אביי in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the term without changing the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עיבור' means the act of lengthening the month, which happens by itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עיבור' means the 30th day. קידוש on that day needs three judges, and after it no קידוש is done.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds רבא's idea that there is no קידוש after the 30th day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who holds the view in רבא's explanation. This sets up the next step, which names the תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that when the new month starts on the 31st, no קידוש is done. The גמרא wants to find a תנא who says this openly.

keyTerms.meaning: And who is it? (Whose opinion is this?)

phrases.english: And who is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבא's explanation in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that no קידוש is done after the day of עיבור.

steps.title: It follows רבי אלעזר בן צדוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this follows רבי אלעזר בן צדוק. He says that if the moon was not seen on time, the court does not sanctify the month, because Heaven already sanctified it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי אלעזר בן צדוק. As it is taught: רבי אלעזר בן צדוק says: If the new moon was not seen at its time, they do not sanctify it, because it was already sanctified in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the תנא behind רבא's explanation and quotes his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the moon was not seen on the 30th day, the new month starts on the 31st anyway. רבי אלעזר בן צדוק says no קידוש is needed then, because Heaven has already set it. This is exactly רבא's idea that 'after עיבור there is no קידוש'.

keyTerms.meaning: Was seen at its expected time
They do not sanctify it
They sanctified it in Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the משנה means that קידוש on the 30th day needs three judges. If the month starts on the 31st, there is no קידוש at all, following רבי אלעזר בן צדוק: 'it was already sanctified in Heaven.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that קידוש by the בית דין matters only when the new month starts on the 30th. When it starts on the 31st, the month begins without any declaration.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok says:
If it was not seen at its time,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the new moon, expected to be seen on the 30th day.

phrases.english: they do not sanctify it,
for they already sanctified it in Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן צָדוֹק הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא's explanation follows רבי אלעזר בן צדוק, who holds that no קידוש is done when the moon was not seen on time.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: קידוש by three judges applies on the 30th day. After that, the month is already sanctified in Heaven.

steps.title: רב נחמן flips רבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says קידוש after the עיבור day needs three judges, and on the עיבור day itself there is no קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Sanctifying the month after the extra day needs three judges. On the extra day itself, there is no sanctification at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a different answer to the problem with the משנה's word 'עיבור'. His answer is the exact opposite of רבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said קידוש happens only on the 30th day (the עיבור day). רב נחמן says the reverse: on the 30th day no קידוש is needed, and on the 31st day, after the month was made full, קידוש is done by three judges.

keyTerms.meaning: The court's formal declaration that the new month has begun
The 30th day of the month, the day that could be added to make the month full
There is not

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבא and רב נחמן. רבא: קידוש only on the 30th day. רב נחמן: no קידוש on the 30th, but קידוש by three on the 31st.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Sanctification after the extra day is done by three;
phrases.notes: 'After the extra day' means the 31st day, once the old month already got its 30th day.

phrases.english: on the day of the extra day, there is no sanctification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a reading of the משנה that is the opposite of רבא's answer in step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבא, קידוש is done only on the 30th day.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עיבור' refers to the month made full. קידוש after it, on the 31st day, needs three judges. On the 30th day there is no קידוש.

steps.title: Whose view matches רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds רב נחמן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier sage agrees with רב נחמן. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's reading of a משנה is stronger if it matches a known תנא. The גמרא now looks for that match.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? (Which תנא holds this view?)

phrases.english: And whose view is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the תנא behind רב נחמן's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that there is no קידוש on the 30th day but there is קידוש afterward.

steps.title: It follows פלימו
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's view matches פלימו, who says a month that comes on time is not sanctified, but a late month is sanctified.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is פלימו, as a ברייתא teaches: פלימו says that if the month comes on time, we do not sanctify it. If it does not come on time, we do sanctify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן follows the תנא פלימו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For פלימו, 'on time' means the 30th day, which is the expected day, so no declaration is needed. A month that starts late, on the 31st, needs a formal קידוש, just as רב נחמן said.

keyTerms.meaning: In its time, the expected day for the new month

steps.confusionAlert: Here פלימו says the opposite of רבי אלעזר בן צדוק from step 10. Each one supports a different אמורא.

phrases.english: It is Peleimo,
as it was taught: Peleimo says:
in its time, we do not sanctify it;
phrases.notes: 'In its time' here means the 30th day, when the new month is expected.

phrases.english: not in its time, we sanctify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן follows פלימו: no קידוש on time, but קידוש when the month is late.

steps.title: רב אשי: the משנה means calculation
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה's 'עיבור החודש' really means calculating the month. It uses the word 'עיבור' only to match 'עיבור השנה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, the משנה is teaching about calculation. What does 'עיבור' mean? The calculation of whether to add the extra day. Since the משנה needed to teach about adding a month to the year, it also used the same word for adding a day to the month.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third way to read the משנה. The three judges are needed to calculate whether the month gets an extra day, not to declare the new month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 had assumed the משנה does not mean חישוב, but רב אשי says it really does ('לעולם חישוב קתני'). This also avoids רבא's problem with אביי, because the word 'עיבור' stays in place. The משנה chose that word so the month and the year would have the same wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Calculation, figuring out when the month should start
Really, actually
Since, because (the משנה was already saying something similar)
Adding a month to the year

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם חִישּׁוּב קָתָנֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Really, it teaches about calculation.
And what is 'עיבור'? The calculation of the extra day.
And since it needed to teach adding to the year,
it also taught 'adding to the month'.
phrases.notes: He means the משנה picked the word 'עיבור' for the month so it would match the wording used for the year.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם חִישּׁוּב קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the משנה, after רבא's and רב נחמן's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the משנה chose its word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עיבור' must mean a court act on the month, such as קידוש.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עיבור החודש' means the calculation about the extra day. The word was chosen to match 'עיבור השנה'.

steps.title: Calculation yes, sanctification no: whose view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that by רב אשי's reading, only the calculation needs three judges and קידוש is not done. It asks who holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Calculating the month, yes, needs three judges. Sanctifying the month, no. Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what רב אשי's reading implies and asks which תנא agrees. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה lists only calculation, it seems there is no formal קידוש of the month at all. The גמרא looks for a תנא who holds that.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
No

phrases.english: Calculation of the month, yes;
sanctification of the month, no.
Whose view is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: חִישּׁוּב חוֹדֶשׁ – אִין, קִידּוּשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ – לָא. מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what רב אשי's reading means and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that months are calculated but never formally sanctified.

steps.title: It follows רבי אליעזר: years are sanctified, not months
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that months are never formally sanctified, whether on time or late. The פסוק speaks only of sanctifying years.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי אליעזר, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says that whether the month comes on time or not on time, we do not sanctify it. The פסוק says 'And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year.' You sanctify years, but you do not sanctify months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב אשי follows רבי אליעזר, who says there is never a formal קידוש for a month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learns from the פסוק that only years get a formal sanctification. So the court's only job for the month is the calculation, which matches רב אשי's reading of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it says (in a פסוק)
The fiftieth year, the יובל

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of 'עיבור החודש בשלשה'. רבא: קידוש on the 30th day (like רבי אלעזר בן צדוק). רב נחמן: קידוש on the 31st day (like פלימו). רב אשי: calculation only, with no קידוש at all (like רבי אליעזר).

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Eliezer,
as it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
whether in its time or not in its time,
we do not sanctify it,
as it says: 'And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year.'
Years you sanctify,
but you do not sanctify months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by naming רבי אליעזר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר: months are never formally sanctified, based on the פסוק about the fiftieth year.

steps.title: Quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next part of the משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view on עיבור השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it starts with three judges, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that עיבור השנה moves through stages of three, five, and seven judges. The גמרא quotes only the opening words before explaining them.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the rest of the quote is left out

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
With three, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה is: begin with three, debate with five, and finish with seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the month and moves to the next view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיבור השנה goes through stages of three, five, and seven judges.

steps.title: The three stages: begin, debate, finish
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the court begins with three, debates with five, and finishes with seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: How does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל mean it? They begin with three judges, debate the matter with five, and finish with seven.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא spells out what each stage in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The numbers are not three separate opinions. They are steps in one process: three judges open the question, five argue it out, and seven make the final decision.

keyTerms.meaning: They begin
They discuss and debate (literally, take and give)
They finish, they decide

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: כֵּיצַד אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: It was taught: How does Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel mean it?
With three they begin,
and with five they debate,
and they finish with seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: כֵּיצַד אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה line quoted in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stages are: three begin, five debate, seven decide.

steps.title: When the first three judges disagree
steps.stepSummary: If one of the first three judges wants to continue and two say no, the single judge is outvoted and the process stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one judge says to sit and discuss, and two say not to sit, the one judge is cancelled because he is the minority.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains what happens at the first stage when the three judges do not agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving on to the stage of five needs a majority of the three. If only one judge wants to go on, the majority rules and the discussion of adding a month ends there.

keyTerms.meaning: To sit, meaning to keep going with the discussion
Cancelled, set aside
A single person in his minority, outvoted

phrases.english: If one says to sit,
and two say not to sit,
the single one is cancelled by being the minority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר לֵישֵׁב, וּשְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים שֶׁלֹּא לֵישֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the case of a split vote at the first stage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the stage of three, if the majority says not to continue, the process ends.

steps.title: A two-to-one vote moves the process to five judges
steps.stepSummary: If two of the first three judges want to go ahead and one does not, two more judges are added and all five discuss the matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two judges say to sit and look into the matter, and one says not to, they add two more judges and debate the question.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from step 19. Now the vote among the first three goes the other way: most of them want to go ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, a lone judge who wanted to continue was outvoted, so nothing happened. Here the majority wants to continue, so the process moves up to the next stage. The court grows from three to five judges.

keyTerms.meaning: To sit, meaning to convene and look into whether the year needs an extra month
They add more judges
Literally 'carry and give': they debate and discuss

phrases.english: If two say to sit,
phrases.notes: 'Sit' here means to meet and look into whether the year needs an extra month.

phrases.english: and one says not to sit,
they add another two judges to them,
and they debate the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים לֵישֵׁב, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לֵישֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite case of step 19: here the majority of the three wants to go ahead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A majority of the three to go ahead brings the court up to five judges, who then debate.

steps.title: Among five judges, a three-to-two vote against stops the process
steps.stepSummary: If two of the five say the year needs an extra month and three say it does not, the majority wins and the year is not extended.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two say the year needs it and three say it does not, the two are cancelled because they are the minority.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now describes how the five judges vote. When most of them say no, the matter ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the five-judge stage, the question is no longer whether to meet but whether the year actually needs another month. A majority against it means the two who wanted it lose. Nothing more is added.

keyTerms.meaning: It needs, meaning the year needs an extra month
They are cancelled because they are the minority

phrases.english: If two say: It needs,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the year. They mean the year needs an extra month.

phrases.english: and three say: It does not need,
the two are cancelled in their minority.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים צְרִיכָה, וּשְׁלֹשָׁה אוֹמְרִים אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the voting rules once there are five judges.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If most of the five say the year does not need a month, the process stops.

steps.title: A three-to-two vote in favor brings the court to seven
steps.stepSummary: If three of the five say the year needs a month, two more judges are added, because a final decision needs at least seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: If three say the year needs it and two say it does not, they add two more judges, because the number may not be fewer than seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the process: a majority in favor among five does not settle it yet. The court must grow to seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'no' vote can end things at five judges, but a 'yes' vote cannot be final at five. Actually making the year longer needs a full group of seven. This matches step 18: start with three, debate with five, finish with seven.

keyTerms.meaning: The required number of judges
Fewer than seven

steps.whatToRemember: Saying 'no' can end the process at any stage. Saying 'yes' needs a full court of seven before the year is made longer.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a three-to-two majority among five is enough to add the month. It is not; two more judges must be added so the final decision has seven.

phrases.english: If three say: It needs,
and two say: It does not need,
they add another two judges to them,
because the required number is not fewer than seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה אוֹמְרִים צְרִיכָה, וּשְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite of step 21: here the majority of the five is in favor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A majority in favor among five sends the matter on to seven judges, the minimum needed to add the month.

steps.title: What do the numbers three, five and seven stand for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what these three numbers of judges are based on.
steps.simpleTranslation: These numbers, three, five and seven: what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks where the pattern of three, five and seven judges comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used three steps of three, five and seven judges without giving a reason. The גמרא wants to know what model these numbers follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Corresponding to what? What is this based on?

phrases.english: These numbers, three, five and seven,
what do they correspond to?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲמִשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעָה, כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the numbers used in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the numbers three, five and seven are modeled on.

steps.title: Two views: ברכת כהנים or the king's officials
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר נחמני and רבי שמעון בן פזי disagree. One says the numbers match ברכת כהנים; the other says they match groups of royal officials named in נביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני and another sage disagree about this. Who is he? רבי שמעון בן פזי. Some say it was רבי שמעון בן פזי and another sage, and that sage was רבי יצחק בר נחמני. One said: they match ברכת כהנים. The other said: three match the guards of the door, five match 'five of those who saw the king's face,' and seven match 'seven who saw the king's face.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two opinions. It gives two versions of the names: in one, רבי יצחק בר נחמני is the main sage and רבי שמעון בן פזי is 'the one with him'; in the other, it is the reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view looks to ברכת כהנים, whose three verses grow from 3 words to 5 to 7. The second view looks to the king's officials: three guards of the door, five who saw the king's face, and seven who saw the king's face. Either way, the court grows in the same steps as a holy or honored group.

keyTerms.meaning: And one other sage who was with him
The blessing the כהנים give the people
Guards of the door
Those who see the king's face, his closest officials

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Naḥmani disagrees about this
with one other sage who was with him.
And who is he? Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
phrases.english: And some say: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi
and one other sage who was with him.
And who is he? Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Naḥmani.
One said: They correspond to the priestly blessing.
phrases.notes: The three verses (במדבר 6:24–26) have 3, 5 and 7 words in Hebrew.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: שְׁלֹשָׁה – כְּנֶגֶד שׁוֹמְרֵי הַסַּף,
phrases.english: And one said: Three correspond to the guards of the door,
five to 'of those who saw the king's face,'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 25:19 lists five such men.

phrases.english: seven to 'those who saw the king's face.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 52:25 tells the same story but lists seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי וְחַד דְּעִימֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the word counts of ברכת כהנים, or the numbers of royal officials in מלכים and ירמיהו.

steps.title: רב יוסף's ברייתא matches the royal officials view
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches a ברייתא saying the three numbers match the guards of the door and the officials who saw the king's face.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: These numbers, three, five and seven: three match the guards of the door, five match 'five of those who saw the king's face,' and seven match 'seven who saw the king's face.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as the second view in step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the second view is not just one אמורא's idea; it appears in a ברייתא. The wording is the same as the second opinion in step 24.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught:
These numbers, three, five and seven:
three correspond to the guards of the door,
five to 'of those who saw the king's face,'
seven to 'those who saw the king's face.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the second view in step 24 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the numbers match the king's officials.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רב יוסף.

steps.title: אביי asks רב יוסף why he never explained this before
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks his teacher רב יוסף why he had not explained the numbers this way until now.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Why, until now, did the master not explain it to us this way?
steps.whatsHappening: A short story begins. אביי, רב יוסף's student, is surprised he is only hearing this explanation now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the law. אביי is asking why his teacher had kept this explanation from them until now.

keyTerms.meaning: Until now
Master, a polite way to speak to one's teacher

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Until now, what is the reason
that the master did not explain it to us this way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A student's reaction to the ברייתא רב יוסף just taught.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב יוסף had not taught this explanation earlier.

steps.title: רב יוסף: I did not know you needed it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that he did not know they needed this, and that he never refused to answer when they asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I did not know that you needed it. Did you ever ask me something and I did not tell you?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי and the other students. He assumed they already knew it, and he reminds them he always answers their questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף was not hiding anything. He thought they already knew the ברייתא. The quiet lesson is that a student has to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: That you needed it
Did you ask me?

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means אביי together with the other students.

phrases.english: I did not know that you needed it.
Did you ever ask me something
and I did not tell you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לָא הֲוָה יָדַעְנָא דִּצְרִיכִיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He did not know they needed it, and he always answered when asked.

steps.title: A memory aid for the next teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives four key words to help remember the order of the coming ברייתות about adding a month to the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Time, נשיא, needs, goat: a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It lists one key word from each of the teachings that are about to come, so the learner can remember their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is a hint to one upcoming teaching. The words are not explained here; their meaning becomes clear as each teaching is quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a list of key words for the coming teachings

steps.confusionAlert: These four words are not a law or a sentence. They are only a list of hints to the teachings that come next.

phrases.english: Time, Nasi, needs, goat: a memory aid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section about עיבור השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A list of four key words for the teachings that come next.

steps.title: A new ברייתא begins: when a year may be extended
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that limits when a year may be made longer. The rest of the sentence continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A year may be extended only...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next teaching, the first one from the memory aid. The sentence stops in the middle and continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'only' tell us a limit is coming. The year can be extended only under a certain condition, which is spelled out next.

keyTerms.meaning: Make the year longer by adding a month
Only, except

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A year may be extended only...

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first teaching listed in the memory aid of step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A year may be extended only under a condition that the ברייתא is about to state.
